purpose: Test whether historically evolved reproductive states alter persistence under the SAME post-switch visitor exposure and demographic bottleneck, and separate viability from realized persistence.
relation_to_precedents: Prompted by the completed four-history common-environment pilot with 512/512 survival and the independent 64-history first-generation viable-output sign switch (global 4/5 gate FAILED). This is a new exploratory stress screen, not a post-hoc revision of the 64-history gate.
switch_protocol: At t=400 sample exactly 8 individuals without replacement from each resident population; apply new capacity 8 and ovule-budget stress for 80 generations, while keeping each plant's full inherited genotype and allowing Mendelian inheritance and mutation. The matched near-history and far-history populations see exactly the same NEW visitor histories for each post near/far arm. No external plant immigration.
readouts: first post-switch expected viable maternal output per plant at bottleneck
first post-switch extinction time; distinguish extinction from endpoint phenotype
mean floral investment and assurance conditional on occupancy
by-environment survival probability and history-paired far-history minus near-history contrast
history-level contrast of evolving vs fixed assurance mode conditional on identical settings
inference: 8 independent visitor histories, two nested demographic repeats; exploratory descriptive with no significance or submission gate. Always report the full 4×2×2×2×4 stress grid, not selected stress slices.
boundaries: Demographic shock is investigator-defined, not a natural disturbance calibrated to an island
New smaller carrying capacity changes density-dependent pollen transfer as well as population size; results are effects of the joint declared switch, not pure carrying capacity
Post-switch ovule_budget is an imposed fecundity cost, not empirically calibrated inbreeding depression
Population disappearance is not rescued by seed immigration (seed supply zero)
Differences arise from historical genotype states and demographic stochasticity; no direct manipulation of which trait evolved first
Any observed difference under the same population bottleneck cannot be called general island rescue without independent confirmation
The 64-history immediate payoff gate failed 1 of 5 predefined tests and remains failed
Never infer future genetic adaptive capacity solely from terminal standing variance
